clue.text: The lower island?

parts.note: surface reading: an island lying lower, nearer sea level, than another
setter's reading: a lower is a cow, a beast that lows, and this Channel Island gave its name to a famous dairy breed

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'lower' as low-er, the animal that moos, not as 'less high'. The island shares its name with a breed of dairy cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is a Channel Island, and a Jersey is a breed of cow, so the island of the mooers.

clue.text: Letters written to one demanding resin

parts.note: the letters L and M spelt out as written words, el and em
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone writes to a person who keeps insisting on gum.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters 'written' are spelt out by their names. 'demanding' has no part in the wordplay and only joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant gum resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Court limits subsidiary activities?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the boundary lines along the long edges of a tennis or basketball court
second meaning: work done in addition to a main job

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court limits' suggests legal restrictions; it is the marked edges of a playing court.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidelines are both boundary markings of a pitch or court and secondary occupations pursued alongside the main one.

clue.text: Submits returns?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: profits or interest produced by an investment

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like filing tax returns; one is the verb to give in, the other the noun for income from investment.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender; yields are the income an investment produces, its returns.

clue.text: Part of the ship aft, possibly — easily damaged

indicators.note: possibly marks the preceding word as one possible arrangement of its letters, not the word itself

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
fragile, easily broken

explanation.surface: A sailor warns that some fitting at the back of the ship is fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aft' looks like part of the description of where on the ship, but it is the fodder. TAFFRAIL is the rail around the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the rail running round the stern of a vessel, so a component of a ship located aft.

clue.text: Where Mr Darling went for a book?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: William Darling, father of Grace Darling, was keeper of the Longstone light off Northumberland
second meaning: a 1927 novel by Virginia Woolf

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Darling suggests the father in Peter Pan; it is Grace Darling's father, the lighthouse keeper whose daughter became a heroine of a sea rescue in 1838.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper goes out to his station on the rock; Woolf's novel of that title is a classic of modernist fiction.

clue.text: Novelist finds another without point

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece stands round the other

parts.note: E. M. Forster, author of A Passage to India, is another novelist
a compass point, east

explanation.surface: One writer discovers a rival who lacks any purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking'; here it means outside. C. S. Forester wrote the Hornblower novels.
explanation.definitionFit: C. S. Forester was a British author of naval adventure fiction, best known for the Hornblower series.

clue.text: Show gets a sound critique

indicators.note: sound means what is heard, so the word is taken as it is spoken rather than as written

parts.note: a critique of a play or book, said out loud

explanation.surface: A theatre production receives a solid write-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'solid' praise; it is the signal to go by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances, a type of stage show.

clue.text: Excites attention when collecting site's rent

indicators.note: collecting means gathering up, so these letters are gathered into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A landlord draws notice when gathering rent for a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money due, and in the surface it is; it is also just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that interests you arouses your curiosity and holds your attention.

clue.text: Law not enforced by late property-owner?

parts.note: the late So-and-so is dead
one who lets property, a landlord

explanation.surface: A deceased landlord's rule nobody now enforces.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical sense of LETTER: not a piece of mail but one who lets.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead letter is a statute still on the books but no longer observed or applied in practice.

clue.text: Vessels returned are some of the first available

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
some of says the answer is a portion of the words that follow, lying inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of 'first' and the start of 'available'

explanation.surface: Containers sent back are among the first ones on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vats are large tanks or tubs for holding liquids, a kind of container or vessel.

clue.text: Remove Gide's old novel

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: the letters as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Take away an old book by André Gide, the French author.
explanation.walkthrough: With Gide named, 'novel' looks like a noun; it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to force it out of its position, which is to remove it.

clue.text: Guides the herd

definitions.meaning: first meaning: directs the course of
second meaning: young castrated bullocks, as a group of cattle

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as someone driving cattle; split it into a verb and a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Steers is both a verb meaning directs and the plural noun for young male cattle raised for beef.

clue.text: Green material?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stretch of mown grass, as a village green or bowling green
second meaning: a fine linen or cotton fabric

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a fabric dyed green; the question mark warns that each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn is a grassy area kept mown, and also a sheer fine cloth used for blouses and handkerchiefs.

clue.text: Hate to be in a crowd standing up in the tea break

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the word is read from the bottom upwards
to break something is to smash it apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
'in' taken as written, 'the' a link
taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone loathes being jammed into a standing crowd at the tea interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea break' reads as a pause for a cuppa; the break acts on the tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to detest or loathe intensely, a stronger synonym for to hate.

clue.text: Impractical person re veals something about ladies' make-up

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: it is a pronoun for any unnamed thing

indicators.note: make-up is how something is composed, so the letters are put together anew

parts.note: the letters as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: A dreamer gives away a secret about women's cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: The page splits 'reveals' as 're veals'; it is only a link. 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but signals the rearrangement, and 'about' puts the pronoun round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist pursues perfect standards over workable ones, the classic unrealistic, unworldly dreamer.

clue.text: City transplant stock, perhaps?

parts.note: the liver is an organ commonly transplanted
a pool is a shared stock or reserve of something

explanation.surface: The City of London's financiers moving shares about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' and 'stock' together suggest the financial district; City here just means a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a major port city on the Mersey in north-west England.

clue.text: Simple barbarian includes bad poems

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Huns were nomadic invaders, the archetypal barbarians

indicators.note: bad means not in proper shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: the letters as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: An uncultured savage's collection contains some dreadful verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and unsophisticated, like cloth woven at home, so simple and unpretentious.

clue.text: Truly ironical

parts.note: surface reading: the word means in truth, indeed
setter's reading: an archaic word for truly now used almost only mockingly

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a dictionary entry: an old word for 'truly' that survives only in ironic use.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsooth originally meant in truth; today it is used facetiously or with scorn, an archaism kept for irony.

clue.text: Number going by sea perhaps in this vessel

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: going suggests moving about, so these letters change places

parts.note: the letters as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: A count of passengers sailing in this ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number going by sea' reads as passengers on a voyage; the number is a Roman numeral, and the sea is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A vase is an open container for flowers, a kind of vessel in the sense of a holder.

clue.text: Moroccan port is to free Mohammedan commander — put-up job

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up turns it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to rid is to free of something
an aga is a commander or chief officer in the Ottoman world

explanation.surface: A Moroccan harbour plots to release a Muslim leader in a staged affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put-up job' means a rigged affair, but in a down clue 'put up' turns letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a city and seaport on Morocco's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Bill comes in to discharge vehicle

indicators.note: comes in to means enters, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to fire is to discharge, as a gun or an employee
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: An invoice arrives for unloading a car.
explanation.walkthrough: A FIACRE is a small four-wheeled horse-drawn cab, once common in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiacre is a hackney carriage, a horse-drawn conveyance for hire, so a vehicle.

clue.text: Part of a trunk or box?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the front of the torso, between neck and abdomen
second meaning: a large strong container with a lid

explanation.walkthrough: A trunk and a box both sound like luggage; the trunk is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The chest is the upper front of the human torso, and also a sturdy lidded storage container.

clue.text: The Pennine way, perhaps?

parts.note: surface reading: the long-distance footpath along the Pennines
setter's reading: any route across those hills is a road over elevated ground

explanation.walkthrough: The Pennines are the upland spine of northern England; a way over them runs at altitude. The usual figurative sense is a main route or an easy course.
explanation.definitionFit: A highroad is a main road, and literally a road that runs over high country like that range of hills.

clue.text: British statesman of the year 1000, possibly

indicators.note: possibly offers one possible rearrangement of the letters before it

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Naming the great politician of the first millennium.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo Amery was a Conservative cabinet minister in the 1920s to 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Amery was a prominent British Conservative politician and colonial secretary, hence a statesman.

clue.text: Female or male comedian?

parts.note: surface reading: asking whether a funny person is a woman or a man
setter's reading: a pantomime role that is a woman but is played by a male comic

explanation.walkthrough: In British Christmas pantomime the comic old woman, the panto dame, is traditionally played by a man in drag.
explanation.definitionFit: The dame is a female character always taken by a male comic actor, so both at once.

clue.text: Perhaps they are paid to play badly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: banknotes handed over in payment

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to pound notes
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to bang out notes heavily on a piano

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like musicians paid to perform poorly. Read as a phrase, 'pound notes' is also what a heavy-handed pianist does.
explanation.definitionFit: Pound notes were the paper currency for a pound; to pound notes is to hammer at a keyboard, playing clumsily.

clue.text: Condemn in so many words?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pass judgment on a convicted person
second meaning: a group of words forming a complete statement

explanation.walkthrough: 'in so many words' is an idiom meaning explicitly; here it splits into a link and a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sentence is to declare a punishment in court; a sentence is a grammatical unit made of several words.

clue.text: Fresh horses in fifty years? Must be wrong!

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters must be set right in another arrangement

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that new mounts were needed only twice a century.
explanation.walkthrough: Relays were teams of fresh horses kept at stages along a coaching route.
explanation.definitionFit: A relay is a set of rested horses ready to replace a tired team on a long journey.
